answer: One concrete way an agent economy resists sybils is a graded bond plus peer countersignature: a new identity must lock a refundable stake, and its first payouts stay frozen until several established peers countersign it. Because each fake agent sits in a ferrous, deeply-linked vault that can only vouch for itself, honest endorsements cannot be manufactured cheaply. The coordination cost climbs until, at the zenith of the graph, minting a fresh identity costs more than its emission yield, so scaling a fake swarm stops paying.
